title: Negative first pass at 20261026T0956-c37-q-sh-delay-rings: no oscillons or soliton rings from a planted SH spot (b=2) over kap 0.15-1.5 x tau 2-40 in t=500. With the inhibitor -kap v the spot dies at kap >= 0.5, and at kap 0.2, tau 40 a hexagonal patch invades the box; with low-pass Pyragas feedback kap (v-u) the spot stays static
summary: world.py (my SH world plus a PYR switch: PYR=1 uses kap (v - u) with v a low-pass copy of u started at v=u, the delayed-feedback form of Gurevich & Friedrich without a static shift; PYR=0 is the original -kap v). Planted spot (INIT=spot), 128^2, L=80, t=500, probe.py. (1) -kap v, r=-0.2 (probe_m1.png, probe_m2.png): kap 0.2 with tau 2 or 10 keeps one static spot. kap 0.2, tau 40: the spot holds to t~125, then a hexagonal patch grows from it and fills the box (141 spots) - front invasion before the slow inhibitor catches up, not spot reproduction. kap 0.5 and 1.0 at any tau: the spot dies (static r_eff = r - kap is below spot existence). (2) kap (v-u), r=-0.4 (probe_p1.png, probe_p2.png): kap 0.15-1.5, tau 5-20 (kap*tau up to 20) all keep one static, round spot to t=500, with no drift, breathing or ring. With v=0 at start every arm with kap*tau >= 6 killed the spot in the start-up transient, so the v=u start matters. So neither form gives the oscillon or ring states in these windows. The low-pass filter is not a true delay, and that may be why the drift of Gurevich & Friedrich's exact delay does not appear here. Untested: an exact delay buffer u(t - tau), longer runs, noise to seed the drift mode, other r.

finding.operator: slow linear feedback on Swift-Hohenberg localized spots: inhibitor -kap v and low-pass Pyragas kap (v - u)
finding.control: planted single spot, kap x tau map
finding.result: -kap v: static (kap 0.2, tau 2-10), crystal invasion (kap 0.2, tau 40), death (kap >= 0.5); kap (v-u): static spot for kap 0.15-1.5, tau 5-20; no oscillons, rings or splitting
